raw_response:
I will keep the farm simple and stay with the local main pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. In Quzhou, this is the normal system, and research from Quzhou itself shows that more than 80% of fields use the winter wheat-summer maize rotation, with most rain falling in summer, so wheat needs the irrigation and maize can mostly follow the rains ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5290742/), [ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0959652614000304), [ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378429025000991)). I am 70, so I will not spread myself across many crops. I want one familiar rotation, machine-friendly work, steady grain, and lower labor risk. I will put all my land into wheat first, then maize after wheat harvest. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, rotary tillage, moderate fertilizer, and two irrigations because that is where water matters most here. For maize, I will direct-seed with no-tillage after wheat, use a hybrid, cut irrigation to one time or only when emergence is weak, and keep pesticide use lower than wheat because summer rain usually supports the crop. I am choosing moderate input levels instead of chasing the highest possible yield, because I care more about stable harvests, lower cash pressure, and work I can still manage myself.
